**Description:** Lists available asset types
**Parameters:** None
**Returns:** Array of asset type strings (e.g., `['hdris', 'textures', 'models']`)

## GET /assets
**Description:** Retrieves assets with metadata and optional filtering
**Parameters:**
- `type` - Filter by asset type (hdris/textures/models/all)
- `categories` - Legacy comma-separated category filter
- `category` - Filter by taxonomy path or URL slug
- `collection` - Filter by collection ID
- `vault` - Filter by vault ID
- `attributes` - Query parameters for asset attributes

**Returns:** Object mapping asset IDs to asset metadata objects

## GET /search
**Description:** "Hybrid semantic + keyword search over asset metadata" with multilingual support
**Parameters:**
- `q` (required) - Search query, max 100 characters
- `t` - Asset type filter
- `future` - Include unpublished scheduled assets
- `min` - Minimum similarity score threshold
- `limit` - Maximum results to return
- `hybrid` - Toggle keyword matching lane

**Returns:** Search results object with ranked asset slugs and relevance scores

## GET /info/{id}
**Description:** Retrieves detailed information for a specific asset
**Parameters:** `id` - Asset unique identifier
**Returns:** Asset object (hdri, texture, or model type)

## GET /files/{id}
**Description:** Lists available file formats and resolutions for an asset
**Parameters:** `id` - Asset unique identifier
**Returns:** File tree organized by resolution and format

## GET /author/{id}
**Description:** Retrieves creator information
**Parameters:** `id` - Author identifier
**Returns:** Author object with name, portfolio link, email, and donation info

## GET /taxonomy
**Description:** Full category taxonomy and attribute schemas for all asset types
**Parameters:** None
**Returns:** Object containing category trees and attribute schemas by type

## GET /taxonomy/{type}
**Description:** Category taxonomy and attributes for a single asset type
**Parameters:** `type` - Asset type (hdris/textures/models)
**Returns:** Taxonomy tree with nested categories and attribute schema

## GET /categories/{type}
**Description:** Legacy endpoint listing categories with asset counts
**Parameters:**
- `type` - Asset type
- `in` - Comma-separated category filter

**Returns:** Object mapping category names to asset counts

# Research Report: Texture Pack / Art Asset Sourcing (Separate from Gameplay Mods)

## 1. OpenGameArt.org

**Active status (2026):** Yes, actively used. The homepage shows a rolling stream of fresh submissions (e.g., "Stone Herringbone Texture (2K)," "Wooden Floors (2K)," "Basic RPG Icons") — https://opengameart.org/. The site ran an "OpenGameArt.org Spring Jam 2026" (March 20 – ~May 5, 2026) cross-hosted on itch.io: https://itch.io/jam/opengameartorg-spring-jam-2026. Similarweb ranks it active but niche (#44,223 globally as of Jan 2026): https://www.similarweb.com/website/opengameart.org/.

**Terms page:** `https://opengameart.org/content/terms-of-service` returns a **404** — that page does not exist. The functional equivalent is the FAQ at https://opengameart.org/content/faq, which states the licenses accepted are: **CC0** ("may be copied, modified, distributed, performed or otherwise used in anyway without asking"), **CC-BY 3.0/4.0** (attribution required, no DRM), **CC-BY-SA 3.0/4.0** (attribution + share-alike, no DRM), **OGA-BY 3.0/4.0** (attribution required, DRM-distribution permitted — this is OGA's own license variant, not a standard CC license), and **GPL 2.0/3.0**. Commercial use is permitted under all of them; the FAQ instructs users to "adhere to the license terms" of whichever single license a multi-licensed asset's uploader chose.

**API:** **No official public API.** Confirmed in the site's own forum: https://opengameart.org/forumtopic/opengameart-api and https://opengameart.org/forumtopic/api. A moderator (MedicineStorm) responded to an API request by pointing to an unofficial third-party project and warning: *"scraping the site could get your IP blocked if it has a detrimental effect on site performance."* No staff-announced API exists as of this research.

**robots.txt (https://opengameart.org/robots.txt):** Standard Drupal robots.txt. Notably includes **`Crawl-delay: 10`** (10 seconds between requests) and disallows admin/system paths (`/admin/`, `/search/`, `/user/login/`, `/user/register/`, etc.) but does **not** blanket-disallow content pages (`/content/*`) or category/search listing pages. So scraping isn't robots.txt-prohibited outright, but (a) the crawl-delay must be honored, and (b) the forum moderator's IP-ban warning functions as an informal ToS-level restriction. Any scraper should self-throttle well beyond the stated 10s delay and identify itself.

**Real license mix observed:** Searching textures directly (https://opengameart.org/art-search-advanced?keys=texture — 3,662 results across 153 pages) shows a genuine mix of **CC0, CC-BY, CC-BY-SA, and GPL-variant** licenses across metal, nature/grass, wood, water/fire, and seamless-texture-pack results — not a single dominant license. This confirms per-asset license-checking is mandatory; you cannot assume CC0 site-wide the way you can with Kenney or Poly Haven.

## 2. Kenney.nl

**License:** Confirmed **CC0** for all asset packs. Kenney's support page (https://kenney.nl/support) states verbatim: *"All game assets on the asset pages are public domain licensed (CC0). You're free to use them, even in commercial projects."* Attribution is optional: *"Attribution is not required, but if you choose to give credit you can do so by mentioning 'Kenney.'"* (Note: `kenney.nl/data/faq` as a URL returned a 404 — the current real page is `/support`.)

**API:** **No API.** Downloads are static asset-pack ZIPs only.

**Download mechanism:** Confirmed by inspecting a real asset page (https://kenney.nl/assets/tiny-battle): the direct download is a **self-hosted, direct-linkable zip URL** with a content-hash-style path, e.g. `https://kenney.nl/media/pages/assets/tiny-battle/c1c25ac1f3-1691487575/kenney_tiny-battle.zip`. This URL pattern (`kenney.nl/media/pages/assets/<slug>/<hash>-<timestamp>/kenney_<slug>.zip`) is stable enough to be scripted per-asset (scrape the asset page HTML for the current hashed link, since the hash changes on updates — it's not a predictable static path). A secondary bulk option exists via itch.io: https://kenney.itch.io/kenney-game-assets ("All-in-1" bundle with automatic updates), which would need itch.io's own download/API mechanics if scripted instead. The asset catalog (https://kenney.nl/assets) is paginated (~14 pages, 16 assets/page) with predictable slugs (`/assets/<name>`), making enumeration straightforward.

## 3. Poly Haven

**License:** Confirmed CC0. https://polyhaven.com/license: *"Once the creator... applies CC0 to a work, the work is no longer his or hers in any meaningful sense under copyright law"* — usable for any purpose including commercial, redistributable, attribution optional (though appreciated). Note the license page also flags that Poly Haven's own site content (logos, renders, text) is separately copyrighted — only the actual asset files are CC0.

**Public API: confirmed real and documented.** Root at https://api.polyhaven.com/ points to Swagger/Redoc docs; the canonical source is https://github.com/Poly-Haven/Public-API (README + `swagger.yml`). No login/API key required, no rate-limit tier, no revenue share, per the repo README and GitHub listing (https://github.com/Poly-Haven/Public-API). Real endpoints pulled from the OpenAPI spec (`swagger.yml`):
- `GET /types` — lists asset types (`hdris`, `textures`, `models`)
- `GET /assets` — filterable by `type`, `category`/`categories`, `collection`, `vault`, `attributes`; returns a map of asset IDs → metadata
- `GET /search?q=` — hybrid semantic + keyword search
- `GET /info/{id}` — full metadata for one asset
- `GET /files/{id}` — **file tree of actual download URLs, formats, and resolutions** for an asset (this is the endpoint a mod-catalog integration would use to pull real texture files programmatically)
- `GET /author/{id}` — author/creator info
- `GET /taxonomy` and `/taxonomy/{type}` — category trees and attribute schemas
- `GET /categories/{type}` — legacy category/asset-count listing

**Scope caveat (important for the report):** Poly Haven is **not primarily a "game texture pack" source** — it's a general 3D-production asset library. Its `textures` type is PBR material scans (diffuse/normal/roughness/displacement maps at multiple resolutions, e.g. 1K–8K) meant for 3D rendering/game-engine materials, not pre-packaged stylized "game texture packs" the way OpenGameArt or Kenney offer. It also hosts HDRIs and 3D models, which are out of scope for a texture-pack catalog specifically. Useful as a high-quality PBR-texture source, not a drop-in "pack" source.

## 4. Standalone CC0 Minecraft Texture Pack Repositories (excluding Modrinth)

**Finding: no credible, actively maintained, standalone CC0 Minecraft texture-pack repository was found.** Specifics:

- **OpenGameArt's own "CC0 Minecraft Inspired Textures" page** (https://opengameart.org/content/cc0-minecraft-inspired-textures) is a single hobbyist submission (posted 2023) of six small 16x16 sprite files the author made for their own mods — not a texture pack, not actively maintained, only 2 favorites.
- **github.com/Null-MC/Oversized** (https://github.com/Null-MC/Oversized) is not CC0 as a whole — the repo explicitly disclaims: *"Textures not owned by me; each is licensed separately."* It's also not a full resource pack but a CTM/OptiFine-dependent texture add-on requiring shader support — wrong shape for a general texture-pack catalog entry.
- **"List of Open License Resource Packs"** (Minecraft Forum, https://www.minecraftforum.net/forums/mapping-and-modding-java-edition/resource-packs/resource-pack-discussion/1256229-list-of-open-license-resource-packs) is a stale ~2014-era thread. None of the listed packs (Pixel Perfection, Coterie Craft, Faithful variants, Soartex, Lumino, Ornate 5) are CC0 outright — most use custom "credit required / no monetization" licenses, several are explicitly discontinued/abandoned, and none are GitHub-hosted, versioned repos suitable for scripted sourcing.
- **madjin/awesome-cc0** (https://github.com/madjin/awesome-cc0) is a general CC0-asset link list, not Minecraft-specific, and would need manual curation to extract anything Minecraft-relevant.

**Conclusion for the report:** flag this explicitly as a gap — there is no equivalent of "Kenney.nl but for CC0 Minecraft texture packs." Modrinth's own resourcepack category (already covered elsewhere per instructions) remains the most viable licensed source for Minecraft-specific packs; anything else found is either non-CC0, unmaintained, or too narrow (single-asset submissions, CTM add-ons) to serve as a catalog source.
